title: The step-by-step game setup a kid or teacher sees after pressing "New game" (buildSetup.*): one question per screen, then a summary, then the Builder opens. Words an 8-year-old can read, sentence case, no emoji. This is the page's name (top of the page and the browser tab). Short.
skipAll: Button at the top of every step: leave the steps and go straight to the Builder (the AI helper). Keep "Builder" as elsewhere on the site. Max ~24 chars.
skip: Button under a step: go on without choosing. Max ~18 chars (three buttons share one row on a phone).
progress: Next to the progress dots. {n} is the step's number, {total} how many steps there are (6).
start.guide: One of two big equal buttons on the first screen: the six steps. Max ~22 chars.
start.direct: The other big button: no steps, straight to the Builder to type an idea. Max ~22 chars.
else.title: The last card on a step: none of ours, the child types an idea of their own. Max ~18 chars.
else.packNote: Shown under the text box when a child types their own game type, world or character. "Packs" are our ready-made worlds and characters. Be honest and kind: the Builder (AI) makes that part itself, so it may look simpler than the ready-made ones.
client.stepNames.type: steps.*.name: the short name of a step, used as a row label on the summary ("Game type: Quiz"). One to three words.
steps.type.placeholder: steps.*.placeholder: grey example text inside the "Something else" box. Two or three short examples after "Like:". Never a real person's or pet's name.
steps.look.title: The question of the 2D or 3D step. Keep "2D" and "3D" as they are.
types.adventure.title: types.*.title: a kind of game, on a card. Max ~18 chars. types.*.text: one short line under it, max ~40 chars (longer text is cut off).
types.duel.text: Two children play against each other on the same phone or computer.
looks.3d.title: looks.*: the three cards of the 2D or 3D step. Keep "3D" and "2D".
looks.auto.title: The child lets the Builder decide between 2D and 3D. Max ~18 chars.
world.preview: Button under each world's picture: opens a big close-up picture of that world. Max ~10 chars.
world.previewLabel: Screen-reader label of that button. {name} is the world's name (studio.worlds.names.*).
client.world.choose: Button in the close-up view: pick this world and close. Max ~20 chars.
client.world.gameAlt: Text for a picture (screen readers): a moment of a game in the 3D world {name}.
client.world.coverAlt: Text for a picture (screen readers): the whole 3D world {name} seen from a distance.
client.world.chosen: Read out by screen readers after "Choose this world". {name} is the world's name.
worlds.sky-islands: worlds.*: one short line about each ready-made 3D world, under its name on a card and in its close-up view. Max ~55 chars (longer text is cut off on the card). The worlds' names are studio.worlds.names.*.
groups.heroes: groups.*: headings over the groups of characters a child can put in their game.
groups.wild: Heading over deer, stag, fox and, later, zoo animals.
chars.soon: A small label beside a group that has no animals yet (dinosaurs, sea animals). Max ~14 chars.
chars.soonText: Under such a group: there are none yet, they will be added later. Never a date.
client.chars.hero: A small line under a person character's name (a knight, a wizard): it can be the player. One word.
client.chars.livesIn: Under an animal's name. {worlds} is one or more 3D world names: the only worlds that have this animal. Short: it is cut after two lines.
client.chars.notIn: Under a character that cannot be picked because the world the child chose does not have it yet. {world} is that world's name.
client.chars.otherWorld: Under a character that cannot be picked because it does not live in the same world as the characters already picked.
learn.math.title: learn.*.title: a school subject on a card, max ~20 chars; learn.*.text: a short line of examples, max ~40 chars.
learn.fun.title: The child wants no learning in the game, only play.
extras.fileTitle: Heading of the box for adding a file: a teacher's worksheet or a page of notes (a PDF or text file).
extras.fileKinds: Under the Choose a file button: which files work here, and that pictures are added later in the Builder. Keep "PDF".
client.extras.removeLabel: Screen-reader label of the Remove button beside a chosen file. {name} is the file's name.
plan.heading: Heading of the summary screen after the six steps.
client.plan.changeLabel: Screen-reader label of a row's Change button. {name} is the step's short name (steps.*.name).
client.plan.decides: The value of a row the child left blank: the Builder will choose. Max ~20 chars.
client.plan.scratch: A small label on a row where the child typed their own idea: the Builder makes that part itself, not from our ready-made packs. Max ~22 chars.
plan.told: Small heading over the sentence that will be sent to the Builder as the child's first message.
plan.open: The big button that ends the steps and opens the Builder with the plan. Max ~22 chars.
client.plan.files: {count} is how many files the child added (1 or 2).
say.start: say.*: short sentences that are joined into the child's first message to the Builder, e.g. "Here is my game plan. Kind of game: Quiz. Make it 3D. World: Castle Quest. In it: Knight and Fox. It teaches: Math." Each must stand alone and end with a full stop. The child reads it before sending.
say.type: {value} is the kind of game (types.*.title, or the child's own words).
say.look3d: Keep "3D" exactly as it is (the Builder looks for it).
say.look2d: Keep "2D" exactly as it is (the Builder looks for it).
say.world: {value} is the world's name (studio.worlds.names.*, or the child's own words).
say.characters: {list} is a list of character names, already joined for your language ("Knight and Fox").
say.learn: {list} is a list of subjects, already joined for your language ("Math and Science").
flatNote: Shown when the child picked 2D and a kind of game that cannot show our ready-made worlds and characters yet (a quiz, a board game...): only running and catching games can, in 2D. Honest, not discouraging. Keep "2D".
chars.soon3d: A small label beside a group of animals that exist for 2D games only so far (the dinosaurs): they are coming to the 3D worlds later. Keep "3D". Max ~20 chars.
client.chars.only2d: Under an animal that cannot be picked for a 3D game because it only exists for 2D games so far. Short (two lines on a small card). Keep "2D".
client.chars.only3d: Under a character that cannot be picked for a 2D game because it only exists in the 3D worlds so far. Keep "3D".
client.chars.youPlay: Under the first character picked for a 2D game: this is the one the child controls; the others they pick are friends who are in the game too. Short (two lines on a small card).
client.all.select: Button in the heading of a group of cards (Farm animals, Heroes, what it teaches): picks every card of that group that can be picked. Max ~14 chars.
client.all.clear: The same button once every card of the group is picked: un-picks that group only. Max ~14 chars.
client.all.selectLabel: Screen-reader label of the Select all button. {name} is the group's name (Farm animals).
client.all.clearLabel: Screen-reader label of the Clear all button. {name} is the group's name.
client.all.picked: Read out by screen readers after Select all. {count} is how many cards are now picked in that group.
client.all.pickedWorld: Read out after Select all in a 3D game when only the characters of one world could be picked together. {count} is how many, {world} the 3D world's name.
client.all.cleared: Read out by screen readers after Clear all.
